BudgetPolicy.description:
A multi-dimensional budget. Every dimension is REQUIRED and separate —
a scalar budget makes the child<=parent comparison undefined across units
(preflight S1a-F5), and a defaultable dimension deserialises to
"unlimited" (S3-05). Units are in the field names.

The same shape serves the workflow root, the per-invocation override and
the agent definition, so the Phase H compiler compares child against
parent DIMENSION BY DIMENSION with no unit conversion.

max_cost_micro_usd.description: Maximum spend in micro-USD (1_000_000 = 1 USD) in scope.

max_total_tokens.description: Maximum total tokens (input + output) across all model calls in scope.

max_turns.description: Maximum agent turns (model-call iterations) in scope.

BudgetPolicy.title: BudgetPolicy.v1

CancellationPolicy.description:
Workflow-wide cancellation policy: which DETERMINISTIC host conditions
cancel the run. No field routes a model output to a cancel — cancellation
authority is host/budget/timeout only (research §12.7; runtime honesty is
Phase J).

allow_host_operator_cancel.description:
The host operator may always cancel; declaring `false` here is
refused by the host (a pack cannot opt out of operator authority —
enforcement is Phase J/L, the field keeps the claim explicit).

cancel_on_budget_exhausted.description: Cancel when any budget dimension is exhausted.

CancellationPolicy.title: CancellationPolicy.v1

CompiledEdge.description:
One edge of the expanded plan, endpoints named by `node_instance_id`
(family 5). Sorted canonically `(from, from_port, to, to_port)` — edge
ORDER carries no meaning in a compiled plan, so the compiler erases it.
CompiledEdge.title: CompiledEdge.v1

CompiledNodeInstance.description: One node occurrence of the expanded plan (family 4).

depth.description: Expansion depth: 0 for the root workflow's nodes.

node.description:
The full normalized node body. Self-contained UP TO pinned
references: node bodies are embedded, while agent definitions,
prompts, schemas and corpora stay pinned BY DIGEST in
`artefact_digests` — the engine executes from the plan and resolves
those digests against the verified pack store, never against loose
source documents.

node_id.description: The template node id inside that workflow.

workflow_id.description: The workflow identity this occurrence belongs to.

CompiledNodeInstance.title: CompiledNodeInstance.v1

CompiledPlacement.description:
Family 7 of `CompiledPlan.v1`. The v1 graph format declares no placement
field (frozen form), so the compiler assigns the most restrictive class to
the whole plan: everything executes on the initiating node (WA-3 — the
run's authority is the initiating node). Per-node placement arrives with
the network verticals as a conscious v1 redefinition.

default_class.description: Placement class applied to every node of this plan.

CompiledPlacement.title: CompiledPlacement.v1

CompilerProfile.description: Family 9 of `CompiledPlan.v1`: which compiler, under which profile.
CompilerProfile.title: CompilerProfile.v1

ContextPolicy.description:
Context minimisation policy: the allowlist of context fields an agent (or a
handoff payload) may receive.

Minimisation is the DEFAULT (research §11.1): everything not named here is
withheld. The allowlist is REQUIRED wherever the type appears — an absent
filter that meant "everything" would reproduce the OpenAI Agents SDK
default this format explicitly rejects (D4: "the handoff never implicitly
transmits the whole history"; preflight B3/S1a-F1).

allowed_context_fields.description:
Names of the context fields allowed through. An empty list is a valid,
maximally-minimised policy (payload-only).

ContextPolicy.title: ContextPolicy.v1

CorpusRef.description: A pinned reference to a knowledge corpus.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned corpus index/manifest bytes.

corpus_id.description: Identity of the corpus, unique within the pack.

CorpusRef.title: CorpusRef.v1

ErrorPolicy.description:
Workflow-wide error policy (declarative; retry semantics land in
Phase K).

max_retries_per_node.description: Retries allowed per node before `on_node_failure` applies. May be 0.

on_node_failure.description: Action once a node's retries are exhausted.

ErrorPolicy.title: ErrorPolicy.v1

JoinPolicy.description:
The explicit fan-in policy of a [`JoinNode`].

Internally tagged like the node roster, with `deny_unknown_fields`
variant bodies, for the same reason: one canonical spelling, no tolerated
junk next to a policy that decides when a barrier opens.

oneOf.description:
First declared source to arrive wins; the rest are discarded. The
exact fit for exclusive routing branches.
oneOf.title: JoinAnyPolicy.v1

oneOf.description: Wait for at least `quorum` of the declared sources.

quorum.description: Minimum number of sources that must arrive, ≥ 1.

oneOf.title: JoinQuorumPolicy.v1

ModelPolicy.description: Model selection and output-shape policy for an agent.

model_id.description:
Model identity the policy names (e.g. `"claude-opus-4-8"`); the
adapter decides how strictly it is honoured (Phase N/O).

provider_class.description: Provider class allowed to serve this agent.

require_structured_output.description:
When true, every model call MUST produce schema-conforming structured
output; a provider that cannot guarantee it is incompatible (§10.5).

ModelPolicy.title: ModelPolicy.v1

NodeFailureAction.description: What happens when a node fails after its retries are exhausted.

oneOf.description:
The failure routes on the node's reserved `error` port (which must
then be wired — Phase H).

PlacementClass.description: The §13.2 placement vocabulary, one canonical kebab spelling per class.

oneOf.description: Execute on the initiating node only.
Prefer local, may fall back to an approved provider.
An approved provider may serve the call.
The SBFB network may serve the call.
The SBFB network must serve the call.

PromptRef.description: A pinned reference to a prompt/instructions artefact.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned prompt file bytes.

prompt_id.description: Identity of the prompt artefact, unique within the pack.

PromptRef.title: PromptRef.v1

ProviderClass.description:
Which class of provider may run this agent's model calls.

Mirrors the adapter phases of the sprint plan: local/cloud model adapters
(Phase N) and the Claude Code / Codex CLI adapters (Phase O). The
provider-vs-structured-output compatibility refusal of research §10.5
("provider incompatible with the model or the structured output") is a
Phase H compiler rule over this declaration.

oneOf.description: Local model runtime (e.g. Ollama on the node).

SchemaRef.description:
A pinned reference to a JSON Schema artefact.

`blake3` carries the `PACK.lock` pin of the schema file. Port compatibility
in v1 is NOMINAL BY DIGEST — two ports are compatible when they pin the
same schema bytes; any richer subtyping rule is a Phase H compiler
decision, not a format property (preflight S1a-F6).

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned schema file bytes.

schema_id.description: Identity of the schema artefact, unique within the pack.

SchemaRef.title: SchemaRef.v1

SubworkflowRef.description: A pinned reference to a child workflow graph.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned child workflow file bytes.

workflow_id.description: Identity of the child workflow, unique within the pack.

SubworkflowRef.title: SubworkflowRef.v1

TimeoutPolicy.description:
Workflow-wide timeout policy. Seconds, non-zero: a zero timeout is not a
disabled timeout, it is nonsense the format refuses at parse.

workflow_timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock ceiling of the whole run, ≥ 1 second.

TimeoutPolicy.title: TimeoutPolicy.v1

WorkflowNode.description:
The CLOSED node roster — an internally-tagged union over the 18 frozen
kinds ([`FROZEN_NODE_KINDS`]). Each variant is a newtype over a dedicated
`deny_unknown_fields` struct, so an unknown field INSIDE a node body is a
parse error (the `unknown_field_rejected_for_every_kind` test measures
this for every kind — serde's internally-tagged deserialisation is
subtle enough that the property is proven, not assumed; preflight S7-A).
An unknown `kind` is refused by the enum itself. No `untagged`, no
aliases: one canonical dotted spelling per kind, because a signed JCS
format cannot afford two byte spellings of one meaning.

schema_ref.description: Pinned schema the incoming payload must satisfy.

field_map.description: Output field name → input field name, copied verbatim.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the accepted payload.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the produced payload.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the payload rendered into the prompt.

model_policy.description: Provider/model policy for this single call.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema the model output must satisfy.

agent_id.description:
Id of the invoked agent; must be declared in the graph's `agent_refs`
(Phase H refusal).

budget.description:
Effective budget of THIS invocation; must not exceed the agent
definition's budget nor the workflow budget (Phase H).

agent_id.description: Id of the specialist agent; must be declared in `agent_refs`.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the bounded sub-task payload.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the result returned to the parent.

context_policy.description:
Context allowlist accompanying the payload. REQUIRED — an absent
filter meaning "everything" is exactly the default this format
rejects (preflight B3).

payload_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the transferred payload. REQUIRED — never optional.

target_agent_id.description:
Id of the receiving agent. When the upstream node is an agent
invocation, the giver's definition must list this target in
`allowed_handoffs` (Phase H refusal).

args_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the call arguments.

capability_ref.description:
Logical capability reference; must appear in the graph's
`capability_requests` (Phase H refusal).

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the call result.
Pinned schema of the result payload.

query_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the query payload.

branch_labels.description:
The closed set of output labels (= output ports). The reserved
`default` port exists in addition and must be wired.

discriminant_field.description:
Name of the payload field whose string value is matched against the
labels.

branch_labels.description:
The closed set of proposable labels (= output ports), plus the
reserved `default` port.

prompt_ref.description: Pinned prompt artefact for the classification call.

branch_labels.description: The static branch labels (= output ports), all activated.

body_subworkflow_ref.description: Pinned child workflow applied to each item.

collection_field.description: Name of the payload field holding the collection to fan out over.

max_cardinality.description:
Structural upper bound on the fan-out, ≥ 1, constant in the signed
graph. Never an expression, never a model output.

source_node_ids.description: Node ids whose outputs this join waits on, statically declared.

body_subworkflow_ref.description: Pinned child workflow executed each iteration.

max_iterations.description:
Structural upper bound on iterations, ≥ 1, constant in the signed
graph.

until_output_flag.description:
Name of the boolean field of the body's output that, when true,
stops the loop before the bound. A deterministic data condition —
never free-form model text.

decision_labels.description: The closed set of decisions the human may take (= output ports).

payload_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the payload presented to the human.
Pinned schema the signal payload must satisfy.

signal_name.description: Static name of the awaited signal.

artifact_name.description:
Name of the artefact, unique among the workflow's outputs and
declared in the graph's `artifact_outputs` (Phase H refusal).

schema_ref.description: Pinned schema the published artefact must satisfy.

CompiledPlan.v1.description:
`CompiledPlan.v1` — the immutable plan produced by the authoritative Rust
compiler (D3/D4). The nine field families of research §12.1, every
collection deterministic. Immutable during a run: editing a draft creates
a NEW plan; it never changes a running one.

artefact_digests.description:
Family 2: exact digests of every pinned artefact the plan touches,
`category → id → blake3` (categories: `workflows`, `agents`,
`prompts`, `schemas`, `tools`, `corpora`, `guardrails`,
`subworkflows`).

capability_closure.description:
Family 3: the CLOSED capability set — `capability_ref → sorted
node_instance_ids` allowed to call it. Nothing outside this map can
ever be granted; membership is DATA for the runtime (per-effect
enforcement binding is Phases J/K/L).

edges.description: Family 5: the normalized wiring, canonically sorted.

entrypoints.description:
Family 5: entry occurrences per scope (`""` = the root scope, else
the expanding occurrence's `node_instance_id`), in pinned-document
order (deterministic; order is authored data, not presentation).

graph_semantic_digest.description:
Family 5 digest: the semantic digest of the normalized graphs
(edges canonically sorted BEFORE digesting — canvas order and
outline order collapse to one digest, WA-T1.2 foundation). Derived
and LINKED to `pack_digest`; never an autonomous integrity surface.

human_gates.description:
§19.3 HITL binding: the `human.review` occurrences of the plan,
sorted — a model output cannot add, remove or reroute one.

node_budgets.description:
Family 6: the declared budget of each budget-carrying occurrence,
already proven ≤ its scope (and ≤ its agent definition) dimension by
dimension.

node_instances.description:
Family 4: every node occurrence, keyed by `node_instance_id`
(RFC 6901 path of node ids, pure function of the structural path).

pack_digest.description:
Family 1: the pack source digest — the authoritative `content`
digest RECOMPUTED from `PACK.lock` (never copied from the claim).

pack_name.description:
Publisher-identity binding (§19.3: a model output cannot change a
publisher): the pack's stable name.

pack_revision.description: Publisher-identity binding: the pack revision this plan derives from.

root_workflow_id.description: The root workflow this plan expands.

scope_budgets.description: Family 6: the budget ceiling of each workflow scope (`""` = root).

CompiledPlan.v1.title: CompiledPlan.v1

EnforcementKind.description:
`Documented` vs `Enforced` — the AM-2 enforcement axis. See the module docs
for the exact meaning: `Enforced` requires a resolvable [`MechanismAnchor`].

oneOf.description: Carried by prompt/process discipline or a bypassable/spec-level check.

A mechanical gate on the authoritative path blocks the process on
violation under normal operation (see the module docs — NOT a claim of
impossible-to-bypass; documented exemptions/scope exist).

MechanismAnchor.description:
Where an `Enforced` element's mechanism lives: a repo-relative `file` and a
`needle` token that must appear inside it. The test layer resolves every
anchor, so an `Enforced` marking whose mechanism vanished fails loudly
instead of lying (P72 anti-score / gate-discriminant discipline).

file.description: Repo-relative path from the workspace root (e.g. a hook or `gates.rs`).

needle.description: A stable token that must be present in `file` for the marking to hold.

ProcessElement.description:
One named element of the process (a role, a mode, a gate, or a hook) with
its enforcement marking, optional mechanism, and the source that declares it.

mechanism.description: Present iff `enforcement == Enforced`; names a resolvable mechanism.

source.description: Which digested source declares this element.

title.description: Short human title from the source.

ProcessInvariants.description:
Boolean process invariants extracted from the sources. Each is a fact the
runtime can assert against, not a knob.

codex_output_rewritable.description:
Codex output is raw, never rewritten by the driver
(`PROCESS.md`; `AGENT_SYSTEM.md §5.3`).

gate_check_is_authority.description:
`gate-check` is a diagnostic, never an authority (`AGENT_SYSTEM.md §2`;
`RRV_FACTORY_CONTRACT.md §2`).

pass_pending_committable.description:
`PASS-PENDING` is never a committable verdict (`PROCESS.md` Phase Commit
Finality; `AGENT_SYSTEM.md §5.2`).

reconciliation_required_before_pass.description:
The final `## Verdict: PASS` is only written after Codex reconciliation
(`AGENT_SYSTEM.md §5.2`).

SourceDigest.description:
The BLAKE3 digest of one source, as embedded in the profile. `blake3` is the
lowercase hex digest of the LF/BOM-canonicalised bytes (see [`canonicalise`]).

blake3.description: Lowercase hex BLAKE3 of the canonicalised source bytes.

SourceId.description:
The authoritative prose sources the profile is extracted from and bound to.
Each variant's [`SourceId::path`] is repo-relative from the workspace root.

oneOf.description:
`docs/agent/PROCESS.md` — the vendor-neutral sprint workflow: the
Guarantee Matrix (`G1`-`G10`), the 9-section commit body, `PASS-PENDING`,
the three verification blocks.

`docs/agent/AGENT_SYSTEM.md` — the role registry (9), the lifecycle modes
(10), the preflight scans, the audit tracks, the gate verdicts.

`docs/agent/RRV_FACTORY_CONTRACT.md` — the authority order
`process > RRV > Factory` and the "no downstream authority" principle.

`docs/factory/FACTORY_GATES.md` — the publication pipeline `FG0`-`FG10`
plus the non-delegable `FG-CSP-authoring`.

`.claude/hooks/phase-precommit-lightcheck.sh` — the mechanical precommit
gate (Phase-A design review, staging coherence, preflight presence, Codex
artifact).

`.claude/hooks/phase-auditor-gate.sh` — the mechanical gate that blocks a
phase commit unless the final review reads `## Verdict: PASS`.

audit_tracks.description:
The nine audit-gate tracks (`AGENT_SYSTEM.md §5.4`). Note: `README §7.1`
Cas A lists an extended 11-track canon (adds `J`/`K` standing); the bound
authority here is `AGENT_SYSTEM.md §5.4`, so the count is 9.

commit_body_sections.description: The nine mandatory commit-body sections (`PROCESS.md` Phase Commit Finality).

process_gates.description:
The process gates `G1`-`G10` (`PROCESS.md` Guarantee Matrix). `G1` and
`G5` are `Enforced` (blocked by the authoritative `agentctl` gate,
mirrored by the Claude lightcheck); the rest — including `G8`, which the
authoritative gate only WARNs — are `Documented`.

publication_gates.description:
The publication gates `FG0`-`FG10` plus `FG-CSP-authoring`
(`FACTORY_GATES.md`). Only `FG-CSP-authoring` is `Enforced` (truly
non-delegable: publish + redeploy); the rest — including `FG8`, which is
skipped on the redeploy path and by the N0 exception — are `Documented`.

sources.description: The BLAKE3 digests of the six sources, in [`SourceId::ALL`] order.

verification_blocks.description: The three full verification blocks (`PROCESS.md` Quality Bar).

FactoryProcessProfile.v1.title: FactoryProcessProfile.v1

CancelOrigin.description:
Who asked for a cancellation. A CLOSED set: cancellation authority is
host/timeout only (`CancellationPolicy` doc, graph.rs) — no variant
exists that a model output could route to, and none carries free-form
text.

`BudgetExhausted` is deliberately ABSENT: real budget consumption is
metered by the real-adapter layer (Phase K) — inventing the variant
before anything can trigger it would be a legacy decoder for a format
that never shipped.

oneOf.description:
The host operator asked. Always honoured: a pack cannot opt out of
operator authority (`allow_host_operator_cancel` is a claim the
engine refuses to let opt out — Phase J enforcement).

The compiled plan's `workflow_timeout_seconds` deadline expired and
its `cancellation_policy.cancel_on_timeout` is set. The deadline is
an ABSOLUTE wall-clock value stored in the durable timer table at
run start — never re-derived on replay.

RunEventKind.description: What happened at one point of a run.

oneOf.description:
An effect is about to be attempted. Written in the SAME transaction
as the outbox row it refers to.

The effect returned a receipt. Written in the SAME transaction as the
outbox row transition to `applied`.

receipt_digest.description: Digest of the receipt — never the receipt itself.

oneOf.description: Every step of the run is memoised and the run is finished.
The run stopped and will not advance.

expected_hash.description:
Digest journaled when the step was intended, when the reason is a
hash divergence. Both hashes are recorded so a post-mortem can be
made from the JOURNAL ALONE: without them only the first caller
ever sees WHAT diverged, and a later `execute` just reports "this
run is terminal". Hex digests carry no payload content.

got_hash.description: Digest re-computed on replay, when the reason is a divergence.

oneOf.description:
A ROUTING decision was taken at the node this entry is about
(Sprint 83 Phase J). The journal records every scheduler decision
that is NOT derivable from plan topology alone, so the reducer
rebuilds control flow WITHOUT parsing any material payload — the
replay-divergence mitigation (THREAT §19): journal the decision
BEFORE acting on it.

`port` is the branch label actually taken: a `switch`/`classifier`
output label (or the reserved `default`), or the engine-internal
`continue`/`stop` verdict of a bounded `repeat` iteration.

port.description: Output port (or repeat verdict) the flow continues on.

oneOf.description:
A `map` node decided its fan-out (Phase J). The cardinality is the
RUNTIME collection size, already proven ≤ the structural
`max_cardinality` of the signed plan — an oversized collection is
refused BEFORE this entry is written, so a journaled fan-out is
always a bounded one.

cardinality.description: Number of child iterations the map dispatched.

oneOf.description:
A `wait.signal` interruption consumed its mono-usage signal
(research §12.6, Phase J). Written in the SAME transaction that
marks the deposited signal consumed — a replayed delivery of the
same nonce can never re-fire the resume.

nonce.description: The engine-derived mono-usage nonce this consumption spent.

payload_digest.description: Digest of the signal payload — never the payload itself.

signal_name.description: Static signal name of the awaited node.

oneOf.description:
A `human.review` interruption consumed its decision (Phase J).
The decision label is validated against the node's closed
`decision_labels` BEFORE this entry is written. The signed HITL
principal/approval binding is Phase L1 — this entry records the
consumption, not an authenticated approval.

decision_label.description: The decision label taken, one of the node's closed set.

nonce.description: The engine-derived mono-usage nonce this consumption spent.

payload_digest.description: Digest of the decision payload — never the payload itself.

oneOf.description:
A cancellation was requested (research §12.7, Phase J). From this
entry on the scheduler emits NO new effect; results of effects
already in flight are kept in the journal but not propagated, and
the run closes as `cancelled`.

origin.description: Who asked — a closed set, never free-form.

TerminalReason.description: Why a run reached a terminal state.

oneOf.description:
A replayed step re-computed a different request hash than the one
memoised. The run stops instead of answering a new question with an
old answer.

An effect was intended against a target that does not declare
idempotency, and the process died before the result was journaled.
The engine cannot know whether the side output happened, so it
reports the honest outcome instead of retrying (which could double
the effect) or inventing a success.

The run was cancelled (research §12.7 honest cancel, Sprint 83
Phase J): emission stopped, in-flight results were KEPT in the
journal but not propagated, and the run closed as cancelled — never
re-labelled completed. The `cancel_requested` journal entry carries
WHO asked ([`CancelOrigin`]); this reason records only the outcome.

RunEvent.v1.description:
One journal entry. Primary key `(run_id, sequence)`.

There is no timestamp: the journal is kept free of any
environment-derived value so an event stream is byte-reproducible across
machines and can be pinned by a golden fixture. (Wall-clock values the
store DOES hold — lease expiry, retention ages — live in state tables,
never in journal rows.)

format_version.description:
Envelope version, written to its own column at append time and READ
BACK from the row. Re-injecting the current constant at read time
would make the field agree with itself forever — a version nobody can
disagree with is not a version. After upcasting, this field still
carries the version the ROW was written under (provenance); only
`kind` is brought to the current shape.

node_instance_id.description: Node instance the entry is about, when it is about one.

request_hash.description: Step request hash, present on the entries that carry a step identity.

RunEvent.v1.title: RunEvent.v1

ApprovalPolicy.description:
When an agent's actions require human approval.

Declarative in v1: the HITL chrome, its signed approval binding and the
sensitive-effect classes are Phase L/L1. `intent` never equals approval

oneOf.description:
No human approval required by this agent's own declaration (host
policy may still require it — layers only ever attenuate).
Approval required before any sensitive effect.

Tool schemas/descriptions are UNTRUSTED CONTENT (D4 point 6, MCP tool
poisoning): pinning them by digest is what makes a poisoned description a
detectable substitution instead of a silent one.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned tool specification file bytes.

tool_id.description: Identity of the tool specification, unique within the pack.

ToolRef.title: ToolRef.v1

SBFBAgentDefinition.v1.description:
`SBFBAgentDefinition.v1` — one bounded agent island (D4). Everything the
runtime needs to hold the agent to its declared bounds, every field
required, every referent pinned by digest.

agent_id.description: Stable identity of the agent, unique within the pack.

agent_version.description: Monotonic version of THIS agent identity.

allowed_handoffs.description:
Agent ids this agent may hand control off to. A handoff node whose
upstream agent does not list its target here is invalid (refused by
the Phase H compiler: "handoff not authorised by the target agent"
family of §10.5). May be empty — most agents hand off to no one.

approval_policy.description: When this agent's actions require human approval.

budget.description:
The agent's own budget ceiling. An `agent.invoke` node declares the
effective per-invocation budget, which must not exceed this (Phase H).

context_policy.description: Context allowlist for this agent's own invocations.

description.description: Human-facing description of the agent's role.

guardrail_refs.description:
Guardrails applied around this agent's calls, pinned by digest. May be
empty.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the payload this agent accepts.

memory_policy.description: Memory scope this agent is allowed.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the output this agent must produce.

tool_refs.description: Tools this agent may use, each pinned by digest. May be empty.

SBFBAgentDefinition.v1.title: SBFBAgentDefinition.v1

PackDigestSet.description:
A single-algorithm digest set, in-toto's `digest` shape.

in-toto allows several algorithms per subject; v1 admits exactly one, BLAKE3,
because a multi-algorithm set invites the weakest-link question ("which one
did the verifier actually check?"). BLAKE3 is not a standardised in-toto
algorithm — the borrowing is of the SHAPE, hence "in-toto style".
PackDigestSet.title: PackDigestSet.v1

PackDigests.description:
The six digests as a signed struct. No member is optional: a missing digest
is a refusal, not a default.

What each one binds, from this crate's point of view: `content` is
RECOMPUTED by the verifier from the lock ([`content_digest_of_lock`]), so it
cannot drift from what the pack pins; `graph_semantic` and `presentation`
are recomputable from a graph document through [`graph_semantic_view`] /
[`presentation_view`]; `compiled_plan`, `evaluation` and `publication` are
validated for SHAPE only here — the documents they cover are lock-pinned
files this crate never opens.

compiled_plan.description: BLAKE3 hex of the compiled plan.

content.description: BLAKE3 hex of every byte pinned by `PACK.lock`.

evaluation.description: BLAKE3 hex of the evaluation suite.

graph_semantic.description: BLAKE3 hex of the presentation-free graph meaning.

presentation.description: BLAKE3 hex of the presentation layer.

publication.description: BLAKE3 hex of the publication metadata.

PackDigests.title: PackDigests.v1

PackLock.description:
`PACK.lock` — every file of the pack pinned by digest.

The signature covers the lock, and the lock names the digest of every byte —
that chain is the rug-pull resistance of the FORMAT. What THIS crate can
enforce ends at the lock: it never sees file bytes, so checking that a
materialised file matches its pinned digest belongs to whoever extracts the
pack. A verifier that skipped that check would re-open the rug-pull.

entries.description: Pinned files, paths unique and sorted by the producer.

PackLock.title: PackLock.v1

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the file bytes.

path.description:
Pack-relative path, forward slashes, no `.` or `..` segment, no drive
letter, no leading separator.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes.

PackProvenance.description: Provenance of the pack, in-toto style.

builder_id.description: Free-form builder identifier, e.g. the tool that assembled the pack.

subject.description: The attested artefacts. At least one, names unique.

PackProvenance.title: PackProvenance.v1

PackSubject.description: One named artefact this pack attests to.

name.description: Name of the artefact, unique within the pack.

PackSubject.title: PackSubject.v1

SBFBPromptAgentPack.v1.description:
`SBFBPromptAgentPack.v1` — root of the signed, portable prompt+agent pack
(D2). NAMES AND PINS — by digest, never by embedding — the workflow graph,
agent definitions, prompts, pinned schemas and evals, and carries requested
(never granted) capabilities and provenance. Documented v1 limitation: the
root does not yet REQUIRE any particular artefact set in its lock (no
role→path rule says "a workflow graph must be pinned") — those requirements
belong to the graph/agent contracts, and until they land a syntactically
valid pack may pin any file set.
Presentation is kept out of the semantic digest by the
[`PRESENTATION_KEYS`] reservation (the kickoff's "`layout/` outside the
semantic digest" intent, realised as reserved member names).

The graph and agent bodies are pinned here BY DIGEST rather than embedded:
`SBFBWorkflowGraph.v1` and `SBFBAgentDefinition.v1` are reserved identities
whose fields are authored in the workflow-language phase, and a root that
embedded them would have to change shape when they land. Pinning by digest
is what lets this root be frozen first.

lock.description: Every file of the pack, pinned by digest.

name.description: Stable identity of the pack, unique per publisher.

pack_revision.description:
Monotonic revision of THIS pack identity, minted by the publisher.

Reserved in v1 so that anti-rollback enforcement has a field to stand on
without a later wire bump. Enforcing it is stateful (a floor per pack
identity, the `iroh_runtime` pattern) and belongs to whoever installs a
pack; this crate is pure and holds no state, so it validates the field's
presence and range, never its history.

requested_capabilities.description:
Capabilities the pack REQUESTS. Requesting is not obtaining: an
authority intersects these against a grant and a policy elsewhere.

secret_refs.description:
Opaque LOGICAL secret references, e.g. `"llm.api_key"` — the format
RULE is that a value here names a slot, never a secret or a
deployment's credential name. Enforcement is shape-heuristic only
(`looks_like_materialised_secret`): a 64-hex secret or one split
across fields walks past it, and the other free-text fields are not
checked at all — the rule stops the honest-mistake paste, nothing
stronger.

SBFBPromptAgentPack.v1.title: SBFBPromptAgentPack.v1

AgentRef.description:
A pinned reference to an agent definition used by this graph.

`blake3` is the `PACK.lock` pin of the agent-definition file. Invoking
nodes name agents by `agent_id`; the closure "every invoked agent is
declared here" is a Phase H refusal.

agent_id.description: Identity of the agent definition, unique within the pack.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned agent-definition file bytes.

AgentRef.title: AgentRef.v1

ArtifactOutput.description: One durable artefact the workflow publishes.

from_node.description: Id of the `output` node that publishes it.

name.description: Artefact name, unique in this workflow.

ArtifactOutput.title: ArtifactOutput.v1

BudgetPolicy.description:
A multi-dimensional budget. Every dimension is REQUIRED and separate —
a scalar budget makes the child<=parent comparison undefined across units
(preflight S1a-F5), and a defaultable dimension deserialises to
"unlimited" (S3-05). Units are in the field names.

The same shape serves the workflow root, the per-invocation override and
the agent definition, so the Phase H compiler compares child against
parent DIMENSION BY DIMENSION with no unit conversion.

max_cost_micro_usd.description: Maximum spend in micro-USD (1_000_000 = 1 USD) in scope.

max_total_tokens.description: Maximum total tokens (input + output) across all model calls in scope.

max_turns.description: Maximum agent turns (model-call iterations) in scope.

BudgetPolicy.title: BudgetPolicy.v1

CancellationPolicy.description:
Workflow-wide cancellation policy: which DETERMINISTIC host conditions
cancel the run. No field routes a model output to a cancel — cancellation
authority is host/budget/timeout only (research §12.7; runtime honesty is
Phase J).

allow_host_operator_cancel.description:
The host operator may always cancel; declaring `false` here is
refused by the host (a pack cannot opt out of operator authority —
enforcement is Phase J/L, the field keeps the claim explicit).

cancel_on_budget_exhausted.description: Cancel when any budget dimension is exhausted.

CancellationPolicy.title: CancellationPolicy.v1

ContextPolicy.description:
Context minimisation policy: the allowlist of context fields an agent (or a
handoff payload) may receive.

Minimisation is the DEFAULT (research §11.1): everything not named here is
withheld. The allowlist is REQUIRED wherever the type appears — an absent
filter that meant "everything" would reproduce the OpenAI Agents SDK
default this format explicitly rejects (D4: "the handoff never implicitly
transmits the whole history"; preflight B3/S1a-F1).

allowed_context_fields.description:
Names of the context fields allowed through. An empty list is a valid,
maximally-minimised policy (payload-only).

ContextPolicy.title: ContextPolicy.v1

CorpusRef.description: A pinned reference to a knowledge corpus.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned corpus index/manifest bytes.

corpus_id.description: Identity of the corpus, unique within the pack.

CorpusRef.title: CorpusRef.v1

ErrorPolicy.description:
Workflow-wide error policy (declarative; retry semantics land in
Phase K).

max_retries_per_node.description: Retries allowed per node before `on_node_failure` applies. May be 0.

on_node_failure.description: Action once a node's retries are exhausted.

ErrorPolicy.title: ErrorPolicy.v1

JoinPolicy.description:
The explicit fan-in policy of a [`JoinNode`].

Internally tagged like the node roster, with `deny_unknown_fields`
variant bodies, for the same reason: one canonical spelling, no tolerated
junk next to a policy that decides when a barrier opens.

oneOf.description:
First declared source to arrive wins; the rest are discarded. The
exact fit for exclusive routing branches.
oneOf.title: JoinAnyPolicy.v1

oneOf.description: Wait for at least `quorum` of the declared sources.

quorum.description: Minimum number of sources that must arrive, ≥ 1.

oneOf.title: JoinQuorumPolicy.v1

ModelPolicy.description: Model selection and output-shape policy for an agent.

model_id.description:
Model identity the policy names (e.g. `"claude-opus-4-8"`); the
adapter decides how strictly it is honoured (Phase N/O).

provider_class.description: Provider class allowed to serve this agent.

require_structured_output.description:
When true, every model call MUST produce schema-conforming structured
output; a provider that cannot guarantee it is incompatible (§10.5).

ModelPolicy.title: ModelPolicy.v1

NodeFailureAction.description: What happens when a node fails after its retries are exhausted.

oneOf.description:
The failure routes on the node's reserved `error` port (which must
then be wired — Phase H).

PromptRef.description: A pinned reference to a prompt/instructions artefact.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned prompt file bytes.

prompt_id.description: Identity of the prompt artefact, unique within the pack.

PromptRef.title: PromptRef.v1

ProviderClass.description:
Which class of provider may run this agent's model calls.

Mirrors the adapter phases of the sprint plan: local/cloud model adapters
(Phase N) and the Claude Code / Codex CLI adapters (Phase O). The
provider-vs-structured-output compatibility refusal of research §10.5
("provider incompatible with the model or the structured output") is a
Phase H compiler rule over this declaration.

oneOf.description: Local model runtime (e.g. Ollama on the node).

SchemaRef.description:
A pinned reference to a JSON Schema artefact.

`blake3` carries the `PACK.lock` pin of the schema file. Port compatibility
in v1 is NOMINAL BY DIGEST — two ports are compatible when they pin the
same schema bytes; any richer subtyping rule is a Phase H compiler
decision, not a format property (preflight S1a-F6).

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned schema file bytes.

schema_id.description: Identity of the schema artefact, unique within the pack.

SchemaRef.title: SchemaRef.v1

SubworkflowRef.description: A pinned reference to a child workflow graph.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 hex of the pinned child workflow file bytes.

workflow_id.description: Identity of the child workflow, unique within the pack.

SubworkflowRef.title: SubworkflowRef.v1

TimeoutPolicy.description:
Workflow-wide timeout policy. Seconds, non-zero: a zero timeout is not a
disabled timeout, it is nonsense the format refuses at parse.

workflow_timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock ceiling of the whole run, ≥ 1 second.

TimeoutPolicy.title: TimeoutPolicy.v1

WorkflowEdge.description: One directed data-flow edge between two node ports.

from_port.description:
Source port. Routing nodes emit on their static labels (plus the
reserved `default`); every other node emits on `out`.

to_port.description: Destination port (`in` unless the destination declares otherwise).

WorkflowEdge.title: WorkflowEdge.v1

WorkflowNode.description:
The CLOSED node roster — an internally-tagged union over the 18 frozen
kinds ([`FROZEN_NODE_KINDS`]). Each variant is a newtype over a dedicated
`deny_unknown_fields` struct, so an unknown field INSIDE a node body is a
parse error (the `unknown_field_rejected_for_every_kind` test measures
this for every kind — serde's internally-tagged deserialisation is
subtle enough that the property is proven, not assumed; preflight S7-A).
An unknown `kind` is refused by the enum itself. No `untagged`, no
aliases: one canonical dotted spelling per kind, because a signed JCS
format cannot afford two byte spellings of one meaning.

schema_ref.description: Pinned schema the incoming payload must satisfy.

field_map.description: Output field name → input field name, copied verbatim.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the accepted payload.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the produced payload.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the payload rendered into the prompt.

model_policy.description: Provider/model policy for this single call.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema the model output must satisfy.

agent_id.description:
Id of the invoked agent; must be declared in the graph's `agent_refs`
(Phase H refusal).

budget.description:
Effective budget of THIS invocation; must not exceed the agent
definition's budget nor the workflow budget (Phase H).

agent_id.description: Id of the specialist agent; must be declared in `agent_refs`.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the bounded sub-task payload.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the result returned to the parent.

context_policy.description:
Context allowlist accompanying the payload. REQUIRED — an absent
filter meaning "everything" is exactly the default this format
rejects (preflight B3).

payload_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the transferred payload. REQUIRED — never optional.

target_agent_id.description:
Id of the receiving agent. When the upstream node is an agent
invocation, the giver's definition must list this target in
`allowed_handoffs` (Phase H refusal).

args_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the call arguments.

capability_ref.description:
Logical capability reference; must appear in the graph's
`capability_requests` (Phase H refusal).

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the call result.
Pinned schema of the result payload.

query_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the query payload.

branch_labels.description:
The closed set of output labels (= output ports). The reserved
`default` port exists in addition and must be wired.

discriminant_field.description:
Name of the payload field whose string value is matched against the
labels.

branch_labels.description:
The closed set of proposable labels (= output ports), plus the
reserved `default` port.

prompt_ref.description: Pinned prompt artefact for the classification call.

branch_labels.description: The static branch labels (= output ports), all activated.

body_subworkflow_ref.description: Pinned child workflow applied to each item.

collection_field.description: Name of the payload field holding the collection to fan out over.

max_cardinality.description:
Structural upper bound on the fan-out, ≥ 1, constant in the signed
graph. Never an expression, never a model output.

source_node_ids.description: Node ids whose outputs this join waits on, statically declared.

body_subworkflow_ref.description: Pinned child workflow executed each iteration.

max_iterations.description:
Structural upper bound on iterations, ≥ 1, constant in the signed
graph.

until_output_flag.description:
Name of the boolean field of the body's output that, when true,
stops the loop before the bound. A deterministic data condition —
never free-form model text.

decision_labels.description: The closed set of decisions the human may take (= output ports).

payload_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the payload presented to the human.
Pinned schema the signal payload must satisfy.

signal_name.description: Static name of the awaited signal.

artifact_name.description:
Name of the artefact, unique among the workflow's outputs and
declared in the graph's `artifact_outputs` (Phase H refusal).

schema_ref.description: Pinned schema the published artefact must satisfy.

SBFBWorkflowGraph.v1.description:
`SBFBWorkflowGraph.v1` — the signed data-flow plan (D4). See the module
doc for the invariants the shape carries.

agent_refs.description: The agents this plan may invoke, pinned by digest.

artifact_outputs.description: The durable artefacts this plan publishes.

budget_policy.description:
The workflow's total budget; every nested budget must fit under it
(Phase H).

capability_requests.description:
Logical capabilities this plan requests; every `capability.call`
must reference one of them (Phase H). Requesting is never obtaining.

description.description: Human-facing description of what the workflow does.

entrypoints.description:
Ids of the nodes where execution starts. Non-emptiness and
reachability are Phase H refusals.

input_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the workflow input.

nodes.description: The nodes, keyed by node id — id uniqueness is structural.

output_schema_ref.description: Pinned schema of the workflow output.

subworkflow_refs.description: The child workflows this plan may run, pinned by digest.

workflow_id.description: Stable logical identity of the workflow.

workflow_version.description: Monotonic version of THIS workflow identity.

SBFBWorkflowGraph.v1.title: SBFBWorkflowGraph.v1

WorkflowPublicProjection.v1.description:
`WorkflowPublicProjection.v1` — the allow-listed public projection of a
workflow consumed by RRV (D1/D4): only whitelisted fields leave the node;
RRV neither launches nor mutates a run. Frontier stub — fields authored in
the publication/RRV phase.
WorkflowPublicProjection.v1.title: WorkflowPublicProjection.v1
